part1.summary:
I built part 1 of the kinds design (the record, the rule module and the check) and committed it as 41a2b11a8e on kinds-build. The tree now holds only that commit. Nothing on the site moves yet, because no bake and no page reads the record.

Every figure matches the design: 38 source keys and 146 M ids are filed in 27 store families. The 6 overlay keys are filed in 2 more families (Jastrow and the Samaritan works). The kind that rests shut covers 14 keys and 27 M ids (25 with rows), 118,674 rows. The name entry covers 1,590 + 92 = 1,682 rows. The store has 652,954 rows. restsOffIds gives the same 27 ids.

Each family's name, shape, its two table cells and its 54 own-word quotes were copied out of the table file by a script, not retyped. Every one was then matched back to the table's bytes: 181 comparisons, none missing. The 5 silent families of the kind are the five the design names.

Addition 1 (which zones rest shut) is now data. A zone rests shut when its own schema_version and route are ZONE_V1 and MAM_RESTORE_V5_SERVE__POSITIONAL_PROTOTYPE, which is the Miqra according to the Masorah restore. restsOffIn answers it. K1 holds it to the disk: it picks exactly the 39 files of data/book-order-v1.json, all of them served. It leaves out the Tikkunei Zohar, the 21 Targum sidecars and the 8 fixtures.

The check runs in about 6.5 s, reading the 256 shards and 69 zones once. On the tree today K1 holds (6 laws judged). K2 prints "not judged: the page does not carry the rule yet" and the check exits 3, which the suite counts apart and never as a pass.

I showed the check refusing 18 wrong states:
- **9 bad records, all K1 red, exit 1:** an unfiled key, a key filed twice, an unknown kind, an overlay family in an entry, an own word that is not a quote, a missing file, a Hebrew letter in a say, the scope moved to the Tikkunei Zohar's route, and a family key the store's index does not name.
- **9 bad page copies, all K2 red, exit 1:** one that ignores the fact, one that reverses the entries' order, one that drops the ids' sort, a loose `is`, a `has` that reads a string as a list, one that reaches outside itself, one opened twice, one never closed, and one that refuses nothing.

A verbatim page copy turns K2 green and the check exits 0 ("the page's text is the module's, line for line"). My first K2 missed the reversed-order and unsorted-ids copies, because today's record cannot tell them apart. I added made-up probe records and a reversed index, and both went red.

Both tools lint with no warnings. Pasted into a copy of the page (zone.html), the block adds one no-unused-vars on `restsOffIds` until part 2 calls it; the rest of the page lint stays at 4/175/9/2.

tools/dictionary-kinds-v1.mjs (imports only node:fs, node:crypto, node:path; nothing from the store reader)

CONSTANTS
- DICTIONARY_KINDS_RULE_ID = "dictionary-kinds-rule-v1-each-dictionary-is-filed-by-what-it-says-it-is-and-a-kind-or-a-category-it-marks-in-its-own-data-may-rest-shut"
- DICTIONARY_KINDS_SCHEMA = "DICTIONARY_KINDS_V1"
- DICTIONARY_KINDS_RECORD = "data/dictionary-kinds-v1.json". This is the path from the reader root: the page fetches `${ROOT}data/dictionary-kinds-v1.json`, and a stamp's `record` names it.

FUNCTIONS
- readKinds(dataDir) -> { rec, sha256, path }.
  - dataDir is the FOLDER HOLDING THE RECORD: reader/data, the same as join(storeDir, "..").
  - It throws one sentence when the record is missing, is not JSON, or kindsFault(rec) is not null.
  - Passing the reader folder refuses, with a sentence saying which folder it wants.
- kindsFault(rec) -> null | string, every fault joined by "; ". It needs no store. It checks:
  - the schema, the rule id, and the version (YYYY-MM-DD plus an optional letter);
  - the kinds: each has a say without a Hebrew letter and its shapes, and no shape sits under two kinds;
  - the families: only known fields; a unique kebab-case id and a unique name; a known kind; a shape the kind gathers; shelf "store" or "overlay" (an overlay family names its folder); non-empty keys, none filed twice in one index; says and where present; every `files` key named in where; each own word a «quote» of says, or `silent` a clause of says;
  - each entry's id, its say (no Hebrew letter) and its ruling;
  - the scope's say, zone (which must name schema_version), how and ruling.
- restsOffIn(rec, zone) -> boolean (addition 1).
  - True when every field of rec.scope.zone equals the zone's own field. Today that is {schema_version:"ZONE_V1", route:"MAM_RESTORE_V5_SERVE__POSITIONAL_PROTOTYPE"}.
  - Ask it of a parsed book zone, never of a sidecar. A Targum commentary (ZONE_COMMENTARY_V2), the Tikkunei Zohar (EDITION_DOOR_SERVE__BUILT_STREAM) and the fixtures (DEMONSTRATION_PASSAGE__INSTRUMENT) answer false.
  - It throws when given an object with no string schema_version.
  - The round's regloss input is named build/round-v1/zones/<b>.baked.bin, so the scope is read from the zone's content, never its file name.
- restsOffOf(rec, mSources, factsOf) -> (row) => entry | null.
  - mSources is the route store's index.m_sources. factsOf is the store reader's factsOf; the page passes its own.
  - It resolves each entry once: kinds -> every store family of that kind; families -> those store families' keys.
  - Per row: m = row[3]. If m is not an own key of mSources the answer is null (overlay ids, MSAM*, PIECE:*, M197, M199).
  - Otherwise it returns the first entry, in rec.rests_off order, whose keys hold mSources[m].key and which either names no fact or whose fact the row carries:
    - with is: factsOf(row)[fact] === is;
    - with has: Array.isArray(v) && v.includes(has);
    - with neither: the fact is truthy.
  - The entry returned is the record's own object: {id, say, ruling, kinds|families, fact?, is?, has?}. Results are memoized per M id.
  - It THROWS at construction, one sentence listing every fault, when:
    - an index key is filed by no store family, or a key is filed by two;
    - an entry names an unknown kind or a non-store (overlay) family, or shuts no store key;
    - an entry has is/has without fact, or both;
    - an entry carries a field outside id, say, kinds, families, fact, is, has, ruling.
  - On the page, catch the throw and treat it as "the record did not hold" (nothing gated, __kindsFailed).
- restsOffIds(rec, mSources) -> string[].
  - The M ids for which a row with no facts rests shut, i.e. whole-source entries.
  - Sorted by length, then code order.
  - Today 27: M1 M2 M6 M10 M15 M16 M21 M22 M28 M32 M34 M37 M42 M43 M48 M53 M57 M61 M62 M64 M73 M76 M81 M87 M94 M138 M194.

PAGE COPY (what K2 lifts and runs)
- zone.html carries restsOffOf and restsOffIds verbatim, without "export": module lines 194-242.
- The copy starts at the line "const restsOffOf = (rec, mSources, factsOf) => {" (any indent, exactly once).
- It ends with the line "// end of the kinds' rule (tools/dictionary-kinds-v1.mjs)" (exactly once).
- Nothing between those two lines may reach outside them. The block uses Object.hasOwn, which the page already uses.

- Header: RUN: tree, GUARDS (the rule id), LEDGER: -.

design_did_not_hold: readKinds takes the data folder, not the reader folder. The design's section 1 says readKinds(readerDir), but its section 3 calls readKinds(join(storeDir, "..")), which is reader/data. I followed section 3. A call with the reader folder refuses with a sentence naming the folder it wants.

own_words is shaped differently from the design's sketch of [{text, where}]. The table gives one 'where' cell per family, so each family carries both table cells byte for byte (says, where), plus own_words as a list of quotes. Each quote is verified to be a «quote» inside says. silent is the table's own clause, verified to be a substring of says, not a composed sentence. files maps each name as the where cell gives it to a path in the tree, and every path exists. This keeps every word the table's and makes K1 mechanical.

Overlay families are keyed by their overlay index's source keys plus the overlay folder, not by M ids, the same way store families are. K1 checks that every overlay key is filed and that every family key is in that overlay's index.
kinds carries shapes, so the mapping from the table's kinds to the lead's is data. K1 refuses a family whose shape its kind does not gather.

The design's K2 method (rows of shut keys plus one row per M id) cannot see two real faults: a reversed entry order and an unsorted restsOffIds. Today's record never has two entries meet on a row, never compares a value with is/has, and the index already lists ids in order. K2 now also runs made-up probe records (two entries over one row; an `is` entry; a `has` entry) and a reversed index, over every row of the store rather than a sample.

restsOffOf throws on an index key that no family files, rather than answering null for it (the house rule: a tool refuses what it does not know). The page's copy throws too, so part 2 must catch the throw and treat the record as not holding.

Consequence of addition 1 for parts 2 and 4: the 21 Targum sidecars (<book>.commentary.bin) are not among the 39, so they keep today's rest and their bakes read the store whole. But they are drawn on 21 Bible books' pages. The page must therefore gate each word by its own zone's rests_off stamp, not by the page's book. Otherwise a Targum word's card would hide what its baked line still reads.

Not filed, because they are packagings rather than dictionaries: the dictionary store, the piece store (its pieces are TAHOT's and MACULA's own, under their keys) and the span store's own two sources (M197, M199). None of them is in the route store index, so restsOffOf answers null for their rows.

page.summary:
I built the page's part of the kinds (the design's parts 2 and 3) in reader/zone.html, together with the fold-ins, and committed it as 2ed036f33f on kinds-build. The tree now holds only part 4's uncommitted tools besides it.

**What the page does now**
- **Where it acts.** Only on a zone that carries emitted_from.rests_off and whose record holds. A zone with no stamp (the Tikkunei Zohar, a Targum, a fixture) draws nothing new.
- **The rule on the page.** The page carries restsOffOf and restsOffIds line for line from tools/dictionary-kinds-v1.mjs. K2 is now judged and green. The page runs them over a copy of the store's own index, taken before the overlays' ids join it.
- **The gate.** It holds shut rows out of the pool after every other gate. It covers the span store's rows too, because they carry their source's own M (Wikidata M2's «the Jewish people» at Exodus 1:1).
- **The card.** It counts what it holds back in pills, in the record's words, with a press. On Genesis 1:22's fifth word it reads «6 from word lists, knowledge bases and encyclopedia titles · show», and opened it reads «6 shut at rest, shown · hide». A card the kinds empty says so, with the same press. A pill an opened dictionary brought wears a dotted edge. A shut reading that was pressed is forgotten when the switch shuts again; forgetPicksWhere now serves two callers.
- **The rail.** A «Shut at rest» block stands above "shelve by". Its switch reads shut | open. The 14 shut source keys are kind-chips, disabled while shut and never .dfp; each chip's title gives the family's own words or the table's silent clause.
- **Reset** shuts the kinds again, only where they act, and leaves the reader's source switches alone.
- **Search** answers what the cards show.
- **The span line** never reads a shut row.
- **The choice is kept** as fh.kinds "open@<record version>"; ?kinds= sets it for one load.
- **No header pill.**

**Port and zones for the proof.** Part 4 had not landed, so I stamped Genesis, Exodus, Amos, Obadiah and Psalms by hand into a scratch overlay and served it on port 8943. Port 8941 was already held by another process (pid 17894, a python http.server serving rt, started 09:15 from scratchpad/v61/critic), and I left it alone. The page before my change was served on 8944. Both of my servers are stopped and the stamped zones are removed. The hand stamp does not bake the line at rest: lines carried by shut rows still read them; span lines are drawn on the page and do follow the gate.

**The proof (K4 by hand)**
- On stamped Genesis all 10 laws hold:
  - fresh reader: kinds shut, 27 ids, sources off MSAM2
  - 6 held back; one press brings exactly those 6, dotted, and fh.kinds is kept
  - a reload stays open
  - reset shuts again, sources untouched
  - 14 chips, disabled while shut
  - 0 live lines at first paint
- The same probe on the old page with the same stamped zone fails 8 laws, so the probe tells a wrong state from a right one.
- **Tikkunei Zohar and unstamped Ruth, old page against new:** the header row, the rail's line, the 41 or 40 chips, the lines of the first three sections and the cards are the same. One card's pointer wording varied between runs; it varies the same way on the old page against itself, so it is a race already there, not this ship.

**Three things the design did not hold, settled by me (figures in the fields)**
1. The design gated the store's rows only. The span store's rows also reach the card, carrying their source's M, so the page gates them too.
2. « · 14 shut» on the rail's line wraps it on a phone, 23px to 52px. I moved it into the line's title.
3. The masthead's name is attested by any dictionary on record, shut or open. Asked of the open ones only, Obadiah fell to "listed in the catalog as obadiah … a proper name will show once a source on record uses one", in lower case, 40px taller. Points 2 and 3 together put the first word at 815, 961 and 936 px on stamped Psalms, Obadiah and Amos (check-contents-shut red). After the change it is 787, 893 and 908 px, the same as unstamped.

**A fault fixed in passing.** railSwitch drew the sources row empty: the word senses pill took Obadiah's strip from 40 chips to 0 until a reload. railSwitch now fills the rows it draws.

**Fold-ins**
- The layout fix is applied (Amos with commentary: 908px).
- The channels' rule is named v3.
- «source» (source-leads) is deleted from toggles-named-v1.json, and /toggles/ is rebuilt.

**Fact for the lead.** Genesis 1:22's card is "tight" at 412×915 and at 1280×1400. Its withheld line folds away there, taking the count and the press with it, as the word senses' press does. On such cards the rail's block is the switch a reader sees.

reader/zone.html, dictionary-kinds-rule-v1 (one RULE line, above the state)

WHEN IT ACTS
- The kinds act only when both hold:
  - zone.emitted_from.rests_off exists;
  - data/dictionary-kinds-v1.json arrives and restsOffOf accepts it over a copy of the store's own index.m_sources, taken before the overlays join.
- When both hold: kindsHere = true.
- When the stamp is there but the record fails: nothing is gated, window.__kindsFailed = true, and window.__kindsFault holds the sentence.
- Fields the page reads from the stamp:
  - .entries[<entry id>].ids {M: n}: the rail's chips, the M ids with n > 0, grouped by source key in the record's family order;
  - .entries[<entry id>].rows: the rail's "N records on this book <say>".
  - No other field is read. Part 4's in-progress regloss writes exactly this shape.

STATE (beside SENSES_KEY)
- KINDS_KEY = "fh.kinds", holding "open@<record version>" or "shut".
- kindsAsked comes from ?kinds=open|shut and lasts one load.
- kindsPref is resolved once the record is here: "open" only when the kept value equals open@<version>.
- Other bindings: KINDS_REC, restsOff (the rule; () => null where nothing acts), RESTS_OFF_IDS, kindsHere, reopenForKinds.
- chooseKinds(id) does nothing unless kindsHere.
- kindsHeldN(pool) gives the number held back; kindsSwitchFor(pool) gives button.kinds-switch[aria-label="dictionaries shut at rest"][aria-pressed].

HOOKS
- window.__kinds: the reader's choice, "shut" or "open". It is set on the Tikkunei Zohar too, where nothing acts.
- window.__kindsHere: true where the gate acts.
- window.__restsOffIds: 27 ids today.
- window.__kindsVersion: the record's version.
- window.__kindsFailed and window.__kindsFault, as above.

POOL (poolFor)
- The gate, kindsHere && !opts.everySource && !opts.everyKind && (kindsPref === "shut" || opts.storeOnly), takes out:
  - routes, after the source switches;
  - extra (span store rows), after the overlays' pointing and stem.
- So the live line (storeOnly) never takes a shut row, open or shut.
- pool.withheldByKind is [{ id, say, n }]: pills, a reading an open group also prints is not counted, each reading counted under the first entry in the record's order, sense openings skipped.
- pool.kindsShown counts the groups standing on shut rows alone; set when open.
- Both ride through carryWithheld and the ketiv/qere weld.
- attributionFor(surface, shown, at, named, everySource, word, everyKind): the masthead passes everyKind = true.

- .kinds-opt[data-kinds="shut"|"open"][aria-pressed].
- p.kinds-entry, one per entry.
